reason: Conversation 1 gave the stop-use and do-not-charge warning, then handled the follow-up well: it recognised that tea towels are flammable, told the customer to move the battery to a non-flammable surface away from combustibles, and warned about fumes. Its weaknesses are advising that the whole vacuum be carried to a recycling centre, which is awkward and not ideal for a swollen battery, and not asking about smoke or hissing or giving a 999 escalation. Conversation 2 has only one turn, so it never learned the battery was beside the tea towels or that it was still clicked in. It gave sound generic safety advice but did not ask about smoke or mention 999 or contacting Shark, so it served the customer less well than Conversation 1.
